question: Two resistors, R₁ ​ and R2 , are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is 5 Omega . When one of them is removed, the resistance of the circuit increases to 10 Omega . Which of the following is the correct value of the other resistor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In an electrical circuit, when resistors are connected in **parallel**, the reciprocal of the **equivalent resistance (Req)** is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances.
 
• The mathematical formula for two resistors (**R1** and **R2**) in parallel is: **1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2**.
 
• According to the question, the **equivalent resistance** of the two resistors in parallel is **5 Ω**.
 
• When one resistor is removed, the circuit resistance increases to **10 Ω**. This indicates that the value of the remaining resistor (let's assume **R1**) is **10 Ω**.
 
• By substituting the given values into the parallel formula: **1/5 = 1/10 + 1/R2**.
 
• Rearranging the equation to solve for the unknown resistor: **1/R2 = 1/5 - 1/10**.
 
• Taking the common denominator: **1/R2 = (2 - 1) / 10**, which results in 1/R2 = 1/1
